`scripts/backup.sh --dry-run SOURCE DEST` now lists every file and directory it would copy plus the dated target, and creates nothing; I ran both modes against a temp directory and the dry run left DEST absent while the normal run copied as before. The flag must come first, before SOURCE.

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST: copy SOURCE into DEST/<date>/
set -eu
dry=
if [ "${1:-}" = --dry-run ]; then
    dry=1
    shift
fi
src=${1:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
dest=${2:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
target=$dest/$(date +%F)
if [ -n "$dry" ]; then
    # list what would be copied, touching nothing
    (cd "$src" && find . ! -name . | sed "s|^\./|would copy $src/|")
    echo "would back up $src to $target"
    exit 0
fi
mkdir -p "$target"
cp -R "$src/." "$target/"
echo "backed up $src to $target"
```

The README's Backup section now shows the `[--dry-run]` usage and describes the option. I left the version alone, so `VERSION`, `app/__init__.py`, the README title and `CHANGELOG.md` still say 1.3.2 with no changelog entry for this.
